transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-30
Start: 14:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Rao (Redwood SE), Liam O'Rourke (Redwood SE); Michael Torres (CTO, Orion Health), Sara Patel (Head of Security), James Lee (Platform Eng), Nina Gomez (Compliance)

Summary: High-level security review focused on encryption at rest and in transit, key management options (Redwood-managed KMS vs BYOK vs HSM/CloudHSM), audit logging, and data residency implications. Customer wants clear path for customer-managed keys and HSM-backed keys for regulated PHI workloads.

Topics: encryption-at-rest, TLS, CMK/DEK, envelope encryption, BYOK, HSM/CloudHSM, key rotation, audit logs, SOC 2 artifacts, data residency

[00:00] Alex Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I can see a full room on the attendee list. Quick agenda: we want to run through our encryption model at rest/in transit, KMS options, BYOK + HSM support and call out any gaps for PHI/compliance. Michael, do you want to kick off with constraints?

[00:18] Michael Torres: Sure, thanks Alex. We are Orion Health so PHI is lot of our data on platform. Main asks: customer-managed keys for at-rest encryption, HSM-backed keys ideally; strict audit logs, SSO + RBAC integrated, and data residency for EU. Also rotation policies — we have internal audit every quarter.

[00:36] Sara Patel: And from security side, we need to see proof — SOC 2, ISO scope, penetration tests or at least attestations. Also: zero-knowledge on Redwood side for keys if we do BYOK, or at least key-wrapping model.

[00:52] Priya Rao: Great — so to start, Redwood encrypts data at rest using envelope encryption: we use a data encryption key (DEK) per shard/tenant that is wrapped by a customer master key (CMK). For hosted customers we provide Redwood-managed CMKs by default. For enterprise we support BYOK — you can bring your CMK in your cloud KMS and we reference it via key ARN, or we can integrate with HSM-backed keys like CloudHSM or Azure Key Vault HSM.

[01:20] James Lee: Wait, when you say "reference" do you have any key material passing to Redwood? We cannot hand raw private keys to vendors.

[01:28] Liam O'Rourke: No, we don't ask for private key material. Our common pattern is key wrap/unwrapped APIs. With BYOK you keep CMK in your KMS — Redwood holds encrypted DEKs and when we need to unwrap we call your KMS (via API) to decrypt the DEK. We can also deploy a VPC-endpoint-only integration so traffic to KMS stays in your cloud.

[01:50] Sara Patel: And for HSMs — does Redwood support CloudHSM for private key operations, or do you require an external gateway?

[01:58] Priya Rao: We support HSM-backed CMKs via the cloud provider's HSM offerings. For AWS that's CloudHSM together with AWS KMS custom key store (KMS-Customer-Managed with CloudHSM). We also have patterns for Azure Key Vault HSM and Google Cloud's HSM. In those setups the CMK is never exportable; Redwood calls the KMS endpoint for wrap/unwrap. There is a short latency impact we can benchmark.

[02:20] Michael Torres: Latency is a concern. We need to know what the per-request penalty looks like when unwrapping DEKs for large batch workflows.

[02:28] Priya Rao: Totally — typical pattern is we minimize round trips by caching unwrapped DEKs in memory in the serving runtime (KV cache), with TTLs aligned to your security needs so we don't call KMS per token. For high-security mode we can set cache TTL to zero which forces KMS calls — that will increase latency and egress KMS ops. We can show numbers in the POC.

[02:52] James Lee: You said KV cache — I think in our notes earlier it got transcribed as K-V cash, ha. But yeah, how do you protect those in-memory keys?

[03:02] Priya Rao: We use memory protection in the runtime and OS-level controls. Also, for Redwood Dedicated or Private deployment we can run in your VPC/on-prem so keys and memory never leave your network. For hosted, we have hardened runtime, SGX-like enclaves are not in prod but we use strict IAM and process isolation.

[03:24] Sara Patel: Is there a hardware enclave offering or FIPS-validated module? Our compliance requires FIPS 140-2/3 for certain ops.

[03:32] Priya Rao: We rely on cloud KMS HSMs which are FIPS-certified. Redwood's runtime itself does not claim FIPS validation; when customers need FIPS at rest ops we recommend BYOK with cloud HSM so the cryptographic operations are performed in FIPS-validated hardware.

[03:50] Alex Chen: I'll flag that for the notes — BYOK + CloudHSM is the pattern to achieve the FIPS requirement.

[04:00] Nina Gomez: About audit logs — we need key usage logs, key rotation history, and KMS request provenance. Do you surface those in the console and as log exports to our SIEM?

[04:10] Liam O'Rourke: Yes — we surface KMS call events and higher-level audit events. For hosted we provide logs through our console and can stream audit logs to your S3 or to your SIEM via secure delivery. For Dedicated/Private deployments logs can stay inside your environment. We also record user-level actions (who requested a key unwrap, service account ids) with timestamps.

[04:36] Sara Patel: And retention — we usually need 7 years for audit trails. Is that supported?

[04:44] Alex Chen: We offer configurable retention windows; 7 years is available as an enterprise add-on. For some customers, we recommend streaming to customer's owned bucket for long-term retention and cold storage.

[04:58] Michael Torres: Data residency — we serve EU data from EU region, but how do you ensure KMS stays in-region?

[05:06] Priya Rao: We support region-scoped CMKs. For BYOK you would create the CMK in the target region and we configure the integration to call that regional KMS endpoint. For Redwood Private or Dedicated in-region deployments, all traffic and keys remain in-region.

[05:20] James Lee: For key rotation, what granularity do you support? Per-tenant DEK rotation? CMK rotation? Automatic rewrap?

[05:28] Priya Rao: We support DEK rotation per-tenant and can do bulk rewrap when CMK rotates. If you rotate the CMK (e.g., scheduled annual rotation or ad-hoc compromise), we perform a rewrap workflow that fetches encrypted DEKs, calls KMS to re-encrypt with the new CMK, and writes them back — we can do this online with negligible downtime but we'll want to validate in the POC.

[05:48] Sara Patel: Can we trigger rotation from our side? We need the ability to rotate keys on demand and see the audit trail.

[05:56] Liam O'Rourke: Yes, with BYOK the customer controls CMK lifecycle in their KMS. Redwood provides APIs to request rewrap operations or we can automate based on CMK rotation events. All operations are logged.

[06:10] Michael Torres: A couple of practical asks: 1) We need step-by-step BYOK integration doc and example terraform for KMS+CloudHSM; 2) We want an estimate of cost impact (KMS API calls + HSM hourly costs); 3) A short performance test showing unwrap latencies and effect of DEK caching.

[06:28] Alex Chen: Good list — we'll send the BYOK runbook and cost guidance. Priya, can you own the perf numbers & sample terraform?

[06:36] Priya Rao: Yes, I'll draft sample Terraform snippets that show KMS custom key store and the CloudHSM cluster setup, plus run a small benchmark with 1k unwraps and with various cache TTLs.

[06:48] Nina Gomez: On the compliance front, we need Redwood's SOC 2 Type II report and evidence of penetration tests. Also SSO integration — SAML or OIDC for RBAC mapping.

[06:58] Alex Chen: We'll share SOC 2 Type II and our pen test summaries — redacted as needed. SSO: we support SAML SSO and SCIM for provisioning. RBAC is role-based in the console with admin/audit/ops roles; for finer granularity we can map teams to roles.

[07:16] James Lee: For private deployments, is the control plane still Redwood-hosted? For some of our customers we need all control plane operations in our VPC.

[07:24] Liam O'Rourke: We have both patterns. Our standard Redwood Private option can run control plane components in your VPC with an optional air-gapped package. In that case you own the KMS and we just integrate into it locally.

[07:36] Sara Patel: Any known gaps? Things we should be wary of?

[07:40] Priya Rao: A couple: 1) Hosted Redwood-managed keys are easiest but don't meet BYOK/HSM requirements. 2) Using BYOK with HSM increases complexity and cost (CloudHSM hourly + KMS API volume). 3) There's a tradeoff between security and latency if you disable DEK caching. We can help quantify those tradeoffs.

[08:00] Michael Torres: On the topic of encryption in transit: do you enforce TLS 1.3? Are there mutual TLS options for service-to-service?

[08:08] Alex Chen: We enforce TLS 1.2+ with TLS 1.3 preferred. For dedicated/private deployments we support mTLS between services; for the hosted API we use strong TLS ciphers and recommend client certs for sensitive integrations.

[08:22] James Lee: Does your SDK verify certificate rotation and pinning? We handle cert rotation with our internal PKI and want to avoid failures during rotation windows.

[08:30] Priya Rao: Our SDKs handle certificate rotation gracefully and use standard trust stores; we can support cert pinning for high-assurance integrations. We'll include a developer note in the runbook.

[08:40] Nina Gomez: A question on data-at-rest encryption for embeddings and logs — are logs encrypted separately?

[08:46] Liam O'Rourke: Logs and telemetry are encrypted at rest with the same envelope model. Customers can opt to stream raw logs to a customer-owned bucket to meet strict retention and audit requirements.

[08:58] Sara Patel: For legal, we need clear contract language about key ownership and breach notification timelines. Can you provide a standard SLA addendum?

[09:06] Alex Chen: Yes, we'll connect legal to provide language for BYOK, key ownership, incident response timelines (72-hour initial notification), and support for evidence collection during audits.

[09:18] Michael Torres: Anything about multi-tenant exposure? We want guarantees that DEKs are tenant-scoped and never reused across customers.

[09:26] Priya Rao: DEKs are generated per-tenant; we don't reuse DEKs across tenants. For extra assurance in Dedicated/Private we can provide architecture diagrams and isolation docs.

[09:38] James Lee: Ok — sample pilot proposal: we spin up a small dataset in EU region, configure BYOK with our AWS KMS (CloudHSM-backed CMK), run sample inference workloads and capture latency/throughput and KMS op counts. Outcomes: verify latency SLO and audit logs.

[09:56] Alex Chen: Sounds perfect. We'll propose a 2-week pilot with defined success criteria: latency within 20% of hosted baseline with caching enabled; full audit log delivery; and successful CMK rotation test.

[10:10] Michael Torres: Timeline-wise we need to have security sign-off by end of January to meet our Q1 rollout. That means a POC in December or early January.

[10:18] Alex Chen: We'll aim to start the pilot second week of December. Action items captured.

[10:26] Priya Rao: Quick note on encryption key compromise scenarios: if a CMK is suspected compromised, we can support immediate key disablement in customer KMS and a forced rewrap of DEKs — we will coordinate with your team and provide forensic logs.

[10:40] Sara Patel: Good — also want to confirm we can get event hooks for key events (rotate/disable) so our SIEM can react in near real-time.

[10:48] Liam O'Rourke: Yes, we can push KMS event webhooks to your endpoint or stream to your event pipeline.

[10:56] James Lee: Any tooling for cost forecasting? CloudHSM costs can be nontrivial.

[11:02] Priya Rao: We'll provide a cost model: estimated KMS API calls per inference, recommended cache TTLs to reduce calls, and sample CloudHSM cluster sizing. We'll include that in the runbook.

[11:12] Michael Torres: Great. Anyone else have questions?

[11:18] Nina Gomez: One more — encryption key escrow? We prefer not to escrow keys with vendors.

[11:24] Alex Chen: We do not escrow customer keys. BYOK means you control the CMK; Redwood holds no plaintext key material.

[11:30] Priya Rao: I'll also call out our limitations: if a customer requests local HSM appliances in an air-gapped environment we can discuss but that's a custom professional services engagement.

[11:40] Alex Chen: Ok — let's wrap with a recap and next steps.

[11:44] Recap (Alex Chen): 1) Redwood supports envelope encryption; BYOK via cloud KMS; HSM-backed CMKs supported (CloudHSM/Azure/Google). 2) DEK caching to balance latency vs KMS ops; per-tenant DEKs and rewrap workflows. 3) Audit logs, retention options (incl. streaming to customer bucket). 4) SSO/SAML + RBAC + SCIM supported. 5) Pilot to validate latency and audit logs with BYOK in EU region.

[12:12] Final steps (Alex Chen): We'll send SOC 2 report, encryption whitepaper, BYOK runbook and sample Terraform, and propose pilot dates. Priya will own the runbook and perf numbers. James to provide KMS topology and rotation cadence.

[12:32] Michael Torres: Sounds good. Thanks all.

[12:36] Alex Chen: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up in email with artifacts and the pilot proposal.

[52:00] End meeting.
